audit.whatIsWrong: Primal Howl is called a suppression and placed at level 6 — "At level 6 he gains Primal Howl suppression", "peel your carries from his Primal Howl suppression", "Primal Howl suppresses you briefly at level 6", "Suppress Tahm Kench with Primal Howl".
audit.why: Primal Howl is Warwick's E, available from level 3, and it is not a suppression: 2.5 seconds of damage reduction that ends (or is re-activated early) in a 1-second FEAR on nearby enemies, cooldown 15/14/13/12/11s. The suppression is Infinite Duress (R), 1.5s, cooldown 110/90/70s. Getting these backwards means the player braces for a suppress at 6 that is actually a fear he can walk out of, and under-rates the real ultimate.
audit.corrected: Primal Howl (E) = 2.5s damage reduction into a 1s fear, 15s at rank 1. Infinite Duress (R) = the 1.5s suppression, 110s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere in the matchup mentions that Infinite Duress is an interruptible channel.
audit.why: This is the single most decisive interaction in the pairing and it is completely absent. Infinite Duress suppresses for 1.5s and the kit flags it channel: "interruptible — any CC cancels it". Tahm Kench carries two cancels: Abyssal Dive's knockup and the Tongue Lash stun at three stacks. The critical caveat the text must carry is that you cannot use either on yourself while suppressed — this only saves an ALLY he ults, or works when a teammate breaks you out.
audit.corrected: When Warwick ults an ally, an Abyssal Dive knockup or a three-stack Tongue Lash stun cancels the channel outright and burns his 110s ultimate for nothing. You cannot do it to save yourself.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect confirmed: zero cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere in the matchup. breakdown.cooldowns says "Track it before every engage" without a single number, and no line tells the player what to wait for.
audit.why: Every trade in this lane keys off Jaws of the Beast: it is his lunge, his damage and his heal on one button, 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s. When it whiffs he has no gap-closer, no sustain and a 15s Primal Howl he has to hold for the disengage. That is a real eight-second window at rank 1 and it is the moment to run the full three-stack pattern. Without the number "track his cooldowns" is not an instruction.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid, content.late, content.whys[4] and content.whys[6] all tell the player to use or hold "Abyssal Voyage" for global threat and repositioning.
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is Tahm Kench's removed pre-2020 W. The live W is Abyssal Dive: a 1000/1050/1100/1150/1200-range dive with a knockup on 21/20/19/18/17s. There is no global tool in the kit. "Never roam below half health without Abyssal Voyage cooldown ready" is advice about an ability that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Abyssal Dive is the escape/engage — short range, knockup, 21s at rank 1 — and it is also one of your two cancels for his ultimate channel.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[2], spikes[1].text, tradeGood and dosFull[1].d all sell a "stun into Devour" / "stun-into-Devour combo" off one set of three stacks.
audit.why: Riot's Tongue Lash text: at 3 stacks "they are stunned and the stacks are consumed". Riot's passive text: "At three stacks, he can use Devour on an enemy champion." One resource, two spenders. The Q stun leaves you with an ultimate you cannot cast. Against Warwick specifically this is the whole trade: Devour is what denies him the Jaws of the Beast heal, and a player who spends the stacks on a stun instead has thrown the punish away.
audit.corrected: Three stacks is one charge. Against Warwick, spend it on Devour — the stun is the worse option here.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (Riot Data Dragon 16.15.1) — P and Q descriptions

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1] is headed "Anti-heal his Q sustain" but its body is the generic three-stack trade line — it never mentions healing or Grievous Wounds. dosFull[2] is headed "Q-stun on 3 stacks" and its body is about him wasting his ultimate.
audit.why: Warwick's healing is the reason anti-heal is core here and the numbers are specific: Jaws of the Beast heals for the damage dealt on an 8s cooldown, and Eternal Hunger heals on every auto below 50% health, TRIPLING below 25%. That last threshold is why chip damage into a low Warwick does nothing without Grievous Wounds.
audit.corrected: Put the healing numbers in the anti-heal do-line and the stack-economy rule in the stack do-line.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.early states "At level 2 he gets Jaws of the Beast".
audit.why: Warwick can take Jaws of the Beast at level 1 — nothing gates it to level 2. Presenting a level-up assumption as a rule is how a Tahm Kench walks into a level-1 lunge while fishing for stacks.
audit.corrected: Read his levelled ability rather than assuming; the useful fact is the 8s cooldown and the whiff window it opens.

audit.why: 53.77% over 755 games. The win chart giving Tahm Kench 5 of 7 stages is consistent with a favourable-but-not-dominant lane; no change needed.

edits.before: Warwick has almost no meaningful level-1 pressure — his passive healing only accelerates when you are below half health, and you are not. Use Tongue Lash aggressively from the start to slow him off CS and begin stacking An Acquired Taste. He cannot out-poke you and he cannot out-sustain Thick Skin poke in short windows. At level 2 he gets Jaws of the Beast, but as long as you are above half health his passive gives him nothing, so keep your HP comfortable and the stacks flowing. By level 3 the stun is online: bait him into a trade, hit the third Tongue Lash, and Devour him — he loses the Q heal he was counting on and takes bonus damage inside you.
edits.after: Warwick has almost no meaningful level-1 pressure — his passive healing only accelerates when you are below half health, and you are not. Use Tongue Lash aggressively from the start to slow him off CS and begin stacking An Acquired Taste. He cannot out-poke you and he cannot out-sustain Thick Skin poke in short windows. Jaws of the Beast is his lunge, his damage and his heal on one button, 8s at rank 1 — step in the moment it whiffs, because above half health his passive gives him nothing. Then land the third Tongue Lash and Devour him — he loses the Q heal he was counting on and takes bonus damage inside you.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are the one window Warwick can cause problems. Blood Hunt's move speed kicks in the moment you dip below half HP, letting him close the gap and chain his Q drain before you can reset Thick Skin grey health. Play this window above half health — activate Thick Skin proactively when you see Blood Hunt's red indicator on you so the shield eats his engage. At level 6 he gains Primal Howl suppression, but you regain Abyssal Voyage for global threat and repositioning. His R suppresses you briefly, but if you have three stacks queued, the stun and Devour are ready the moment the suppress ends — he traded his ultimate to set up your combo.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are the one window Warwick can cause problems. Play this window above half health — activate Thick Skin proactively when you see Blood Hunt's red indicator on you so the shield eats his engage. Primal Howl is his E, not his ult: 2.5s of damage reduction ending in a 1s fear, back every 15s. Level 6 brings Infinite Duress, a 1.5s suppress on 110s — ride it out with three stacks banked and Devour is ready the instant it drops.

edits.before: At first item your Heartsteel or Sunfire Aegis sustain overtakes whatever Warwick built — his drain-based healing cannot match your grey health conversion in a long fight, and he has no way to burst you fast enough to outpace Thick Skin. In teamfights you peel your carries from his Primal Howl suppression by sitting between him and them, using Tongue Lash to slow his chase and Devour to yank him away from a suppressed ally. At two items the lane is effectively over in your favour; Warwick can still win isolated skirmishes if you let him catch you at low HP with Blood Hunt active, so never roam below half health without Abyssal Voyage cooldown ready.

edits.after: Three An Acquired Taste stacks buy the Q stun or Devour, not both — Devour is the one that denies Warwick the Jaws of the Beast heal he needs to survive.

notes: Packet defect "NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere" is addressed with real numbers from the kit: Jaws of the Beast 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s, Primal Howl 15/14/13/12/11s, Blood Hunt 80/70/60/50/40s, Infinite Duress 110/90/70s. Also note the six suspectNames entries in the packet for this matchup are ALL false positives — "Tongue Lash's", "Three An Acquired Taste", "Stack An Acquired Taste", "Use Tongue Lash", "Blood Hunt's", "Thick Skin's" are correct names with prefixes/suffixes. The detector missed the two errors that actually matter here (Primal Howl described as a suppression, and Abyssal Voyage), because neither is within edit distance of a live ability name.
